notes: REPLACES AN AMOSTOOLS STUB. Until 2026-08-12 this row held only the token table with the library stripped out from under it -- both length fields zero, no code, every routine word overwritten with `====` -- so the tier could not rise above `manual`. The real library's table is IDENTICAL to the stub's, entry for entry, id for id and spec for spec, which is a check on the AMOSTools reader as much as on this registration. What changes is that the code is now here to read. THE LIBRARY IS CALLED `SBASE_EX` -- not a .lib, and not named for the product. The archive's own Installer script settles it: `(set #libname "SBASE_EX")` then `(set #newlibname "AmosPro_SymBase.Lib")`, so the file is renamed on the way in. It was found by its token table, which opens `db se`, `db us`, `db addres`, `db clos` with the high bit on each name's last character as AMOS stores them. DBENCH AND SYMBASE ARE THE SAME PRODUCT AT TWO AGES, both by Lázár Zoltán. dbench-0.42's 24 keywords are symbase-0.94's first 24, in the same order, with the same ids -- `db sel`, `db use`, `db address`, `db close`, `db flen`, `db fieldno`, `db saved on`, `db saved off` and on. Neither should be ported without the other open. SymBase 0.92's readme records a keyword REMOVAL -- "REM: Date functions removed to a separate extension / No more needs date.library" -- which is exactly the shape that makes one build's tokens detokenise to nonsense under another, so the `renumbered` verdict may apply across the family and has not been checked. FOUR VERSIONS ARE HELD and the earlier three are what make the renumbering question answerable: 0.58 is a third the size of 0.85, so something large changed between them. The stub collection had all four token tables; the real 0.94 binary is the one registered.  ALSO IN THE ARCHIVE: Comp/SymBase/Tools/ -- Create, Dedit, DSort, Index, Server and Client, all compiled AMOS programs, with Examples/BOOKSHELF and its source. `Libs/gui.library` (46,948 bytes) is there because the tools need it; that is the GUI family's back-end, not SymBase's, and it is the first copy of it in the corpus.
